content.en: National Investment & Manufacturing Zones (NIMZ) are specialized industrial townships established under the **National Manufacturing Policy (NMP)**. These zones are conceived as integrated industrial cities with world-class infrastructure, land use on a large scale, and clean, energy-efficient technology. They are designed to provide a conducive environment for manufacturing units to thrive, thereby contributing to the **Indian Economy** by increasing the manufacturing sector's share in GDP to 25% and creating 100 million additional jobs.

definition.en: Provision of high-quality physical infrastructure including roads, power, water, and waste management.
definition.hi: Provision of high-quality physical infrastructure including roads, power, water, and waste management.

content.en: Each NIMZ is managed by an SPV, which is a corporate body responsible for the development and management of the zone.

content.en: Students often confuse NIMZs with SEZs; remember that NIMZs are focused on manufacturing and industrial growth, whereas SEZs are primarily export-oriented.

content.en: Focus on the role of NIMZs in the context of the 'Make in India' initiative for Mains answer writing.
